name: Conservative signal-propagation direction rules
semantics: Within the ontology layer, a rule source_class -> target_class supports removal of the reverse traversal for a supported undirected edge. Positive KinasePredictor kinase-to-substrate evidence and mapped OmniPath source-to-target records supply additional ordered relationships without changing the undirected edge posterior.
conflict_policy: Unique ontology directions are applied first. For ontology-unresolved pairs, unique KinasePredictor kinase-to-substrate directions are applied next. OmniPath can uniquely orient only pairs left unresolved by both earlier layers. A later source cannot reopen or reverse an earlier disallowed traversal. Bidirectional evidence remains unresolved, and all source conflicts are retained in the audit.
sign_policy: Direction and biochemical sign are separate. These rules orient possible propagation but do not label activation or inhibition.

external_direction_policy.rule: Mapped source-target records support their reported direction. A unique ontology or KinasePredictor orientation remains in force. OmniPath uniquely orients only pairs that both earlier layers left unresolved, so it can add a disallowed reverse traversal but cannot reopen or reverse an earlier disallowed traversal. Opposing source directions are recorded for audit. If OmniPath records occur in both directions for an otherwise unresolved pair, both traversals are retained.
external_direction_policy.consensus_direction_usage: The OmniPath consensus_direction flag is retained for audit but is not required; agreement of all mapped directed records for a pair is the operational criterion.
external_direction_policy.effect_on_probability: None. The permitted traversal retains the undirected edge probability and only a uniquely disallowed reverse traversal is set to zero.

kinase_predictor_direction_policy.source: Observed-site KinasePredictor top-ten predictions selected in the active edge-evidence configuration
kinase_predictor_direction_policy.rule: When both the aggregate KinasePredictor Bayes factor for an ordered kinase-to-substrate relationship and the stream's complete undirected pair Bayes factor exceed one under the run's Tq and negative-evidence settings, kinase -> substrate is permitted and substrate -> kinase is removed unless a unique ontology rule already controls the pair. Bidirectional supported predictions do not orient an otherwise unresolved pair.
kinase_predictor_direction_policy.effect_on_probability: None. KinasePredictor still contributes to one symmetric edge-existence posterior. Its retained kinase and substrate roles are used only to set the disallowed reverse traversal to zero in the propagation matrix.
kinase_predictor_direction_policy.path_effect: A path cannot cross a resolved fork or collider by traversing a KinasePredictor-supported phosphorylation edge backwards.

rules.rationale: A receptor ligand or signaling-receptor-binding entity is treated as acting on the receptor.
A regulator of receptor activity is treated as acting on the receptor.
Per the project rule, a kinase-binding protein does not propagate toward the connected kinase; the retained direction is kinase to binding protein.

rules.basis: project propagation policy by kinase/phosphatase symmetry
rules.rationale: The requested kinase-binding rule is applied analogously to phosphatase-binding proteins.
A GTPase regulator, exchange factor, or activating protein is treated as acting on its connected GTPase.
Adenylate and guanylate cyclases produce cyclic-nucleotide second messengers.
Phosphatidylinositol phospholipase C activity produces lipid-derived second-messenger signals.
Nitric-oxide synthase produces the second messenger nitric oxide.
A cyclic-nucleotide phosphodiesterase acts on and decreases its connected cyclic-nucleotide second messenger; sign is recorded but not yet used in path scoring.
A second messenger is treated as acting on a connected protein annotated for cyclic-nucleotide or calmodulin binding.

classes_without_standalone_direction.reason: A broad process annotation identifies participation but not causal order.
A broad regulation annotation does not identify which connected node is regulated.
Adaptor/scaffold activity supports assembly or proximity but does not by itself establish signal-flow direction.
